business_rules.statement: Agents are records, not code. One agent-record schema exists; every agent, platform-authored or tenant-composed, is an instance of it with nine fields.

The governance-binding field's declared values are `authoring-time policy`, `runtime human gate`, and `none — reasoning agent`; the Prevention Agent carries the first, the Deviation and Containment Agent the second for proposals beyond pre-authorised containment, and the Shift Handoff Agent and every tenant-composed agent the third.
An agent definition whose runs are on the record cannot be deleted; its history must remain explicable.
A tenant retention value looser than the floor is rejected at the point of entry with the bound stated, rather than accepted and logged.
business_rules.enforcement_point: floor register at point of entry

business_rules.statement: Retention-value changes, for the horizon or a bound, for any tenant, are critical class requiring root approval.
Only approved content enters the corpus; the agent selects only from what the quality team sanctioned; embeddings change how an asset is found, never whether it was approved.
There is no path by which an agent acquires a tool at runtime that its record does not name.
business_rules.enforcement_point: capability scope on the agent record

business_rules.statement: A residency-affecting provider change is a critical-class change requiring root approval.
The evaluation gate sits after approval rather than before it, so an approved change that fails a scenario still does not ship and the prior version stays in force.
business_rules.applies_to: prompt, model config, provider config changes

business_rules.statement: Three initiation forms exist and only three: a deterministic trigger; a schedule, for the Shift Handoff Agent; and an explicit human request — Command Center action number nine, Supervisor and above.
An activation with no antecedent in one of the three initiation forms is rejected and raised as an incident.
Feedback on agent outputs is always optional and one tap — never required, never gating.
The evaluation-pass gate for a composed agent is hard and platform-wide; four gates stand between composition and production, each returning to composition rather than forward.
The launch builder composes reasoning agents only. Action agents ship as platform-provided templates the tenant configures rather than composes. Tenant-composed action agents are deferred.
Approving a newly composed agent for live use is an authoring-time control and never appears in the Command Center gate queue.
There is no artificial-intelligence model on a device at V1; nothing in the source describes on-device inference, an embedded model, or model distribution to a device.
A rollback may never restore a state in which a capability acts without passing its current evaluation scenarios, and may never re-base an in-flight run.
Rule one — removal from active use never permits deletion of required evidence or audit history.
Rule two — artificial intelligence may never remove or rewrite its own audit history: may not delete, may not modify, may not cause an audit record not to be written.
An administrative or operational change and its audit event commit in the same transaction, so an action that cannot be audited does not happen.
Deletion occurs only where a named compliance standard requires it, with the list of those standards owed by the client.
Anonymisation is the platform's one irreversible act; measurement, result and evidence survive and identity becomes an opaque worker identifier.
No claim of 100 per cent coverage is made while an open decision remains.

No artificial-intelligence model sits in the deviation-triggering path, anywhere, online or offline. Detection is deterministic; interpretation is agentic. Agents activate only after a deterministic trigger.

Severity classification happens on-device at the instant of capture, including fully offline, and a Severity 1 classification places the lot hold at once without waiting for connectivity. Only delivery of escalation waits for sync.
Artificial intelligence may never release a Severity 1 hold. Release is Quality Manager only, uniformly, and arrives at the device as a lot-release command on the command channel.
No platform-level pause of the agentic layer ever suppresses the on-device deterministic layer. The deterministic backbone is not agent machinery and has no off switch.

Nothing a worker sees is machine-translated at runtime. Coaching content and Work Instructions render from authored English and Spanish variants carried in versioned locale files and in the Workflow package.
No surface may imply that an offline tablet received or applied anything. Commands are applied at the device's next sync, in order. There is no real-time remote control of a worker mid-run.
Do not describe AVIIXA as having artificial intelligence that works offline. At V1 it does not, and the Statement of Work does not ask for it.

The absolute rule: cached approved guidance (PROV-3) and deterministic rules (PROV-4) are never, on any surface, in any locale, under any failure condition, labelled or described as live artificial intelligence.
business_rules.enforcement_point: rendering contract lint plus runtime assertion

business_rules.statement: A second absolute rule: artificial intelligence is advisory unless the source explicitly grants execution authority; nothing an agent proposes reaches a worker or changes a record without a human gate or pre-authorised policy.
On-device artificial intelligence must never be the only path for safety-critical functionality; a local model would sit strictly beside layer (c)'s absence, never inside layer (a).

A local model may never classify a deviation, set or alter a severity band, place or release a hold, decide a gate, decide a qualification, alter a specification limit, or write to the official record.
Asking for help is never a gate and never blocks progression; a queued request is never presented as sent, delivered, or answered.
A delayed answer is advisory and must be revalidated against context that has since changed. It can never instruct, override a gate, alter a classification, or release a hold.
A confirmation shown before a durable commit is a lie the platform cannot retract; the local write commits before any user-visible confirmation appears.
Queued artificial-intelligence requests upload strictly after the captures they reference.
Requests never carry a Severity, never trigger containment, and never appear in the Anomaly Register. They are advisory objects and must not be able to imitate safety objects.
`reconciled` is the only state that guarantees the request appears in the execution record; every other terminal state must transition into it.
No state may be inferred from the absence of another. A request that is `uploaded` is not `processing` until the server says so.
An artificial-intelligence answer is always the lowest-priority payload on the command channel; the five safety command classes always precede advisory content.
No artificial-intelligence failure of any kind may affect the deterministic layer, and no artificial-intelligence failure may cause data loss.
Output that fails validation is suppressed, never rendered with a caveat.
Partial output is quarantined rather than published: retained with its trace for engineering and audit, excluded from every official record, summary and export, never discarded.
No artificial-intelligence capability can be enabled while any governing value in the open register is unset, and no register value has a code-level default that would apply silently.
Retrieval never ranks over an unfiltered corpus; the metadata filter is applied before ranking and a filter failure suspends retrieval rather than degrading it.
An incident cannot be closed while any dependent view or derived data set remains un-recomputed.

No number a supervisor may have acted on is ever silently rewritten; recompute is itself an audited event where late data materially changes headline figures, with materiality defaulting to any change to a severity count.
A device presented with a package failing signature or version verification refuses to open the run, records the refusal, and takes no capture.
Escalation creation and escalation delivery are distinct, separately timestamped states; no surface renders creation as delivery.
Escalation routing names roles and never named individuals.
A quota state never suppresses the on-device deterministic layer.
A gate item never times out into action; a timeout escalates only, and a gate with nobody on shift remains open and human-decidable indefinitely.
Resume after an emergency pause is always a separate audited act and never happens automatically.
AIMODE-16 Recovery complete cannot be entered while any queued capture, queued artificial-intelligence request, or unrecomputed aggregate remains outstanding for the affected scope.
AIMODE-04 cannot be entered by any device while DEC-ONDEVICE-001 remains undecided, enforced by configuration rather than by convention.
Every user-visible guidance element on every surface resolves to exactly one of the six provenance classes, with no element unclassified and no element carrying two.
An element classified PROV-1 that cannot produce an agent run identifier and a decision record fails closed to PROV-6.
Every artificial-intelligence-derived field is always in exactly one of four labelled states — complete, pending, stale, failed; blank is never rendered.
The Reviewer is never the Author, under every failure condition, with no bypass introduced by any degraded path.
Publication is blocked with every blocking condition named specifically and linked to its remedy; a generic refusal is a defect.

Every console action commits with its audit event; access to any tenant's operational content requires one of the three named access classes and is mirrored to the tenant's audit stream; no ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console.
An asset that consistently fails to resolve difficulties is flagged for the Quality Manager to review or retire.

options: (a) bind the horizon to the record-finish window

decisions.question: Does on-device artificial intelligence enter scope at all?

workflows.name: Composed agent — composition to deployment (eight numbered steps)
workflows.trigger: Agent Author composes a reasoning agent in the Studio Agent Builder

workflows.name: Chapter 42 — how the connectivity boundary is exercised end to end (eight steps)
workflows.trigger: A run is assigned and the version-pinned Workflow package downloads
terminal_states: Reconciled into the execution record and the tenant audit log

workflows.name: Worker asks for help while offline — the twenty-two-step behaviour
workflows.trigger: The worker taps the help control on the current step while offline

workflows.name: Chapter 43 — how a failure is handled end to end (eight steps)
terminal_states: Incident closed after recovery and reconciliation

workflows.name: Provider-layer failure workflow (nine steps)
workflows.trigger: A model call fails or exceeds its deadline
terminal_states: Deterministic fallback for every affected tenant

workflows.name: Orchestration failure workflow (seven steps)
workflows.trigger: The loop exceeds a bound — plan steps, replans, tool-call budget, or the loop timeout

workflows.name: Retrieval failure workflow (eight steps)
workflows.trigger: The agent requests retrieval with its metadata filter

workflows.name: Governance-layer failure workflow (seven steps)
workflows.trigger: A governance control fires: evaluation failure, gate timeout, pause, suspension, or rollback
terminal_states: Reconciliation records what did not happen

workflows.name: Edge (connectivity/device) failure workflow (six steps)
workflows.trigger: The condition is detected at the device or at the server
terminal_states: Recovery on reconnection, reconciliation ordered by server receipt

contradictions.description: DEC-GATE-001: §3.7 and §6.6.1 read Prevention Agent coaching as entirely pre-authorised policy; §8.3.2 and §8.3.3 read every action agent as routing through a human gate.
conflicting_values: pre-authorised policy (§3.7, §6.6.1)
runtime human gate for every action agent (§8.3.2, §8.3.3)

contradictions.description: DEC-AIEMBED-001: §5.7.2 names Gemini Embedding 2.0 as the current embedding model while §8.4.1 states learning is model-agnostic by construction and §8.7.1 makes embedding one of four swappable router roles.
conflicting_values: embedding model is swappable like any router role
an embedding index is coherent only within one model's vector space, so substitution is a migration requiring full re-index

contradictions.description: DEC-AIFALLBACK-001: §5.7.2 states each screen or failure type keeps a curated fallback asset per locale, reading as an obligation; §5.11 and §5.12 do not list a missing curated default among publication blockers and §8.7.3's completeness check covers locale packs only.
conflicting_values: missing offline fallback blocks publication
missing offline fallback does not block publication

contradictions.description: DEC-AIDISCLOSE-001: §8.7.5 and §6.9.3 place AI-availability disclosure on the Command Center; §7.12 and §7.19 name no worker-facing indicator, while §1.3's honesty principle argues for one.
conflicting_values: disclosure is a Command Center concern; the worker simply sees no card
the honesty principle applies with equal force to the worker

contradictions.description: DEC-CAP-001: §5.5.3 names seven capture types (including dropdown selection) while §1.7 and §7.8.3 name measurement, scan, photo, checklist, boolean, e-signature and free text.
conflicting_values: §5.5.3 seven types including dropdown selection
§1.7 and §7.8.3 set naming checklist and boolean

contradictions.description: DEC-SYNC-001: safety argues commands should apply before capture upload; data integrity argues captures must upload first. Both readings stay on the record.
conflicting_values: commands first
captures first
adopted: stop-class commands, then full capture upload, then enabling classes

contradictions.description: DEC-AIHELP-001: the source describes coaching as agent-initiated on an authored timing trigger (§5.2.1, §7.12) and never describes a worker asking; the blueprint commission requires a defined worker-initiated offline help behaviour.
conflicting_values: agent-push only, as scoped
worker-pull required by the commission

contradictions.description: DEC-LANEB-001: the Studio's three-stage approval chain versus Lane B auto-publish remains unresolved and is preserved without resolution.
conflicting_values: three-stage approval
Lane B auto-publish

contradictions.description: DEC-AGENTLC-001: §8.3.5 says agents generally are migration-managed with evaluation-gated, approval-cycled enable/disable, but that statement is made for platform-authored agents while a tenant-composed agent is deployed by the tenant's own chain.
conflicting_values: platform console approval cycle governs enable/disable
tenant workspace deployment by the tenant chain

contradictions.description: Prompts as an object: the blueprint commission names prompts with a lifecycle while the Statement of Work never describes prompts, their authorship, versioning or governance.
conflicting_values: commission requires a prompt lifecycle
Not specified in the Statement of Work

contradictions.description: Confidence policies: the blueprint commission names confidence policies as an object with a lifecycle and the Statement of Work contains no such concept anywhere.
conflicting_values: commission names confidence policies as an object
Not specified in the Statement of Work — no confidence concept exists

contradictions.description: Two different things are called routing and must not be conflated: model routing is a platform setting, escalation routing is tenant-authored Studio content.
conflicting_values: model routing — four router roles, platform setting
escalation routing — tenant-scoped Studio record naming roles

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Agent definition and policy lifecycle failure — excessive grants, broken reference, partial distribution, enablement with a failing scenario
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Refuse publication on a broken reference; refuse enablement on a failing scenario
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The prior version remains in force; then disable the agent leaving the deterministic layer and human paths intact
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Prior approved policy in force, agent disabled if necessary, nothing lost
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Republication; per-device in-force state confirmed against the published version

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Prompt, model and provider configuration failure — binding applied without re-evaluation, provider outage, residency-violating binding
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Fallback router role
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Degraded routing with the artifact marked; then agent unavailability with the honest tenant flag
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Prior binding in force, or agents unavailable, with the deterministic layer untouched
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Rebind and re-evaluate; traces checked to carry correct binding attribution

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Tool permission, memory configuration and retrieval source failure — grant wider than reviewed, sub-floor retention attempt, index rebuild failure, erasure under legal hold
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Refuse the out-of-bound value; serve the curated default while the index rebuilds
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No coaching, difficulty recorded; then agent unavailability with the honest flag
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Prior approved state in force; nothing lost
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-index and reinstatement; selectable-asset set reconciled against the approved set

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Evaluation suite, routing policy and quota failure — scenario weakened without approval, routing template propagation, quota without ceiling behaviour, metering gap
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Refuse the change; apply the prior version
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Nobody-on-shift escalation default for routing; agent unavailability for quotas; then emergency pause where the platform cannot establish which capabilities are properly gated
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Prior approved state in force; deterministic layer running; humans holding every authority
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Corrected object approved; every enabled capability checked against a passing suite at its current version

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Request, recommendation, draft, output and feedback failure — activation with no antecedent, wrong audience, draft published without review, offline delivery rendered as delivered
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Reject the invalid activation; hold the output in its queued state honestly
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Deliver a degraded artifact naming its gaps; then record an explicit non-production event
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The human works from the raw record; nothing is falsely rendered as delivered or approved
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-assembly or replay per DEC-REPLAY-001; every trigger reconciled to an activation or explicit non-activation

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Composed-agent lifecycle failure — excessive memory grants, misleading artifact, no owner after turnover, disablement with no defined mechanism, in-flight run at disablement
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Return with reasons at either review stage
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Per-tenant emergency pause — the only currently specified way to stop a composed agent; then disable the atoms it depends on (blunt, last resort)
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Composed agent unable to act; no operational behaviour lost; standard agents and deterministic layer unaffected
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Resubmission; every deployed composed agent reconciled to an approval record and a current passing suite

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Incident, package and rollback-version failure — incident not flagged, partial distribution, unevaluated severity table distributed, rollback re-basing an in-flight run, closure without a note
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-distribute; re-raise the flag
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Prior pinned package remains in force on any device that did not receive the new version; then the Command Center shows per-device in-force state honestly
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Every device operating on an approved, evaluated package version; the deterministic layer intact everywhere
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Confirmed distribution and incident closure; per-device package inventory reconciled against the published version set

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Evidence and audit integrity failure — effect outside the audited transaction, orphan cleanup removing evidence, tiering treated as deletion, erasure under legal hold, agent granted a modify path
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Refuse the operation
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Halt the offending job and raise a platform incident; then emergency pause of agent activity while the integrity question is open
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No further effects; records frozen; deterministic layer running; humans holding every authority
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Root cause fixed, records reconciled, integrity verified; mismatches enumerated and reported rather than repaired silently

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Working memory lost mid-run — run-context assertion (Major)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Abandon the run
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Curated default asset then deterministic only
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Next trigger starts a fresh run; failed activation recorded

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Memory write failure after a successful output — write acknowledgement missing (Minor)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry the write
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Store restored; Lane A learning signals reconciled and unrecorded outcomes flagged

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Profile-memory redaction failure — redaction assertion before write (Critical)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Discard the write; the unredacted candidate is never stored
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Redaction fix, approval-cycled; privacy incident recorded

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Cross-tenant retrieval attempt detected — tenant-scope assertion on every retrieval (Critical)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Suspend retrieval platform-wide for that path; every candidate discarded; the event is a security incident
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Engineering fix plus a security review; full audit of the window — isolation is an enforced invariant with no off switch

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Instruction-shaped content detected in worker free text or an uploaded asset — guardrail classification (Major)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Proceed with the content treated strictly as data
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Guardrail tuning; attempt rate monitored as a security signal

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Evaluation failing for an enabled capability — drift canary suite run on cadence (Critical)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Cached guidance
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Scenario fixed and the suite passes; outputs in the failing window reviewed by the Quality Manager

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Evaluation harness itself unavailable — harness health probe (Critical)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Existing enabled capabilities keep running; no new enablement
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Deterministic only if the harness loss cascades
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Harness restored; the enablement queue drained in order once checks resume

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Gate item times out unacknowledged — gate timer, ten minutes Severity 1 and thirty minutes otherwise (Major)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Escalation per the tenant's routing
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Fallback delivery to the Quality Manager role
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Gate open and human-decidable; no action taken
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A human decides; timer breaches recorded as gate-health metrics

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Nobody holding the target role on shift — role resolution returns empty (Major)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Fallback delivery to the Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, visibly marked
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Gate remains open indefinitely rather than timing out into action
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A human decides; fallback deliveries counted; DEC-NOSHIFT-001 remains open

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Emergency pause, platform-wide — pause state (Critical)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Cached guidance
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Resume as a separate audited critical-class act; parked runs listed, none resume automatically

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Emergency pause, per tenant — pause state (Major)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Cached guidance
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Resume as a separate audited act; parked runs listed for that tenant

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Tenant suspension intersecting an agent run — suspension state (Critical for compliance suspension, Major otherwise)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Soft: operations continue in full; hard: the enumerated completion pipeline; compliance: immediate lock with data preserved
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Compliance case: device locked, all local data preserved, fixed message 'Operation suspended. Contact your supervisor. Your work has been saved.'
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Suspension lifted per its state machine; soft-state exit is an explicit operator signal under DEC-SUSP-001

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Approval chain unavailable for a Lane-B proposal — no approver-capable role reachable (Major)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The proposal waits; nothing is applied
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Stale flag at thirty days, still waiting
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No change to any configured value
failures_fallbacks.recovery: An approver decides; proposal aging reported

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Lane-B auto-published patch fails distribution — package distribution acknowledgement missing (Major)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The device keeps its pinned version, which is always safe
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Runs execute on their pinned version
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Distribution retried; per-device package inventory reconciled against the published version

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Model or package rollback while outputs are in flight — rollback initiated with active runs (Major)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Prior version continues serving
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Target version passes evaluation and serves; outputs attributed to the version that produced them, no silent reattribution

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Device offline at answer delivery — delivery attempt with no device session (Minor)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Hold the answer server-side
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Surface it in the Client Command Center drill instead
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The answer is retained, never delivered to a phantom device
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Device returns; delivery state recorded honestly, nothing claims delivery

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Device offline beyond the credential-trust window — window expiry against last successful sync (Major)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Forced sync before designated high-risk actions
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Restrict to steps that require no fresh authority
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Run parks; the worker continues other assigned runs
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Sync completes; credential freshness recorded

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Command backlog with advisory content queued behind safety commands — queue inspection at sync (Minor)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Apply safety commands first, advisory last
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Advisory content expires per DEC-AISTALE-001 rather than blocking
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Backlog drains; command states traversed distinctly, never collapsed into applied

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Duplicate delivery of the same answer — idempotency key collision (Minor)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Discard the duplicate
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Idempotency restored; duplicate rate monitored

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Clock skew beyond threshold on the requesting device — skew guard, default about five minutes, ceiling sixty (Major)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Server-receipt ordering, which is already authoritative
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Route conflicts to the Client Command Center conflict-and-skew review
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Clock corrected; conflicts resolved by human review, never by an untrusted clock

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Device storage full, request cannot be queued — write failure on the durable queue (Major)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Refuse the queueing action with a plain message
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Captures and evidence retain priority over advisory data
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Storage freed after confirmed receipt plus integrity check; DEC-STORE-001 remains open

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Work package invalid, unsigned, or version-mismatched — signature and version verification at run open (Critical)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Refuse to open the run
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Worker reassigned to another run by the Supervisor
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No capture is taken against unverified content
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Package re-pulled; the refused period recorded so the record gap has an explanation

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Device wiped or de-authorised with queued requests pending — wipe command with a non-empty queue (Critical)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Final sync attempt of pending captures and queued requests
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the device never returns, the answer and request remain server-side against the run record
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Device returns or is written off; DEC-WIPE-001 remains open

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Partial output persisted before failure — output present with no completion marker (Major)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Suppress and fall back to cached guidance
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Engineering fix; quarantined artifacts enumerated in the incident report

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Answer arrives after the run finished — delivery attempt against a finished run (Minor)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Deliver as advisory against the closed record
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Record without delivery where the device never returns
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The finished record is not modified by the answer
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The answer appears in the record as an advisory artifact, not as a correction

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Answer arrives after worker substitution — assignment changed between ask and answer (Major)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Route to the original worker's record
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Surface in the Client Command Center for the Supervisor
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Pre-substitution steps remain attributed to the original worker
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Attribution preserved; the substitute is never shown another worker's answer

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Answer arrives after a Severity 1 hold was placed — hold present on the scope at delivery (Major)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Deliver with the hold-precedence banner
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Suppress if the hold scope makes the answer misleading
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The hold stands; only the Quality Manager releases it
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Hold released by the Quality Manager; the answer recorded against the deviation, not against the release decision

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Reconciliation mismatch between trace, decision record, and operational record — count comparison at reconciliation (Critical)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Freeze reconciliation and raise for review
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Manual reconciliation by the platform team
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No record is altered until the mismatch is explained
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Root cause fixed; append-only annotations record what was corrected, by whom, and when

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Technical recovery complete but dashboards still stale — component healthy while a dependent view has not recomputed (Major)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Show the stale marker with its true age
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The view is honest about being behind
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Recompute completes; the incident cannot close while any dependent view is stale
